season_garden_05_001.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_001.text: By the fifth garden afternoon, the new ordinary shade was standing in the permitted court. Its supports had been fitted and checked by the responsible maintenance team during their own appointment. Staff had posted its weather limits and kept the seating position inside the approved area. Yue first noticed the change as a softer patch of light on the bench. The blue bird looked less fierce beneath it. Beyond the wall, qualified tree workers had removed the damaged crown, leaving the old closed area awaiting its remaining ground checks.

season_garden_05_002.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_002.text: The empty sky above the former tree site surprised her more than the fallen branch had. With the crown gone, the wall seemed shorter and the kitchen window too exposed. Qiu stopped beside her and looked up. Neither spoke for a while. A clean removal could make a loss clearer. The workers had done necessary safe work, and the absence still hurt the people who had used that shade. Yue let the two facts sit together while the side entrance filled with the ordinary smell of simmering greens.

season_garden_05_003.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_05_003.text: “I thought removing the danger would make the garden feel better immediately,” Qiu said. “It feels stranger.” Yue asked whether the old crown's presence had made her imagine restoration remained possible. Qiu nodded, then frowned at the answer's neatness. “Perhaps. Or I simply knew where to look for the sky.” She turned toward the permitted court. The new shelter did a real useful job. It had not replaced the old arrangement of branches in a person's sight, and it could not be expected to do so.

season_garden_05_004.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_004.text: The bench owner was sweeping the dining hall's doorway. She said the tree workers had told her when the crown was gone, as she had asked. She had chosen not to watch the cuts. Her adult son had walked with her afterward to the safe viewing point staff permitted. They had both been quiet on the way back. Today she wanted the younger people to stop looking at her every time they noticed the gap. “I notice it too,” she said. “I am still trying to finish the floor.”

season_garden_05_005.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_005.text: Yue apologized for hovering and offered to fetch the light dustpan if the woman wanted it. She did. Qiu moved their own small tool bag out of the sweeping line. The correction was ordinary and a little embarrassing. They had made attentiveness into another way of asking the woman to display grief. Her floor needed clearing, and her sadness did not have to become available whenever a visitor saw the sky. When the doorway was clean, she invited them to see how the blue bird looked in shade.

season_garden_05_006.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_006.text: It looked almost green from one angle. Qiu wanted to investigate the pigment and the changed light. The owner wanted to enjoy the surprise. Yue said the bird could have two colors without requiring a work report. Qiu gave her a mock-offended look, then sat in the available chair rather than on the bench reserved for the owner at that moment. Their humor had become more comfortable without promising a relation beyond the choices they actually maintained. The garden gave them occasions to share a joke, and room to leave it there.

season_garden_05_007.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_007.text: The gardener's new planting plan concerned a small visible bed in the safe court, separate from the still-unreleased old tree ground. He offered two viable uses within the actual water and maintenance available: a modest patch of seasonal flowering annuals, or one young plum supplied and planted by qualified garden staff. Annuals could offer color within this season if they germinated and grew under the observed conditions. The young tree would not provide this season's missing shade. Either option needed its own agreed care beyond the helpers' light preparation.

season_garden_05_008.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_008.text: The material prices were stated before any selection: three copper for the approved annual seed and suitable light planting materials, or eight copper for the suitable young plum and its required planting materials under staff's plan. Both fitted the thirty-four copper remaining in the garden materials allowance. Purchase would occur only after the chosen option was actually accepted, stock confirmed and the responsible treasurer authorized its stated amount. Neither woman would advance personal money as a hidden donation or make the old trial grant reappear to cover the difference.

season_garden_05_009.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_009.text: The existing garden staff could maintain either modest option within their actual ordinary rota and water plan after the helpers' ten-week arrangement ended. The gardener described that accepted responsibility and its realistic limits, including how failed germination or a tree that did not establish would be handled as a present finding rather than a personal debt of the helpers. Yue did not volunteer the next year of her life to make a tree promise sound beautiful. Qiu did not promise that flowering would succeed because she had chosen the quicker-looking option.

season_garden_05_010.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_05_010.text: “I would like color somebody can see from the room this summer,” Qiu said. “There are people who may not come back next year.” The sentence struck Yue harder than the planting plan had. It was true without being a prediction about a particular patient. Yue looked toward the quiet hall. Her preference for patient growth sometimes borrowed a future that another person could not safely assume. She asked the gardener how early color might realistically appear under the annual plan, and what uncertainty remained even with good care.

season_garden_05_011.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_011.text: The gardener gave the actual seasonal estimate and the ordinary reasons it might fail: unsuitable weather, seed losses, interrupted water or pests. He would not guarantee flowers by a visitor's requested date. Qiu listened, then asked whether a few existing safe nonmedicinal potted flowers could be displayed while the selected bed established, if their owner agreed and the route stayed clear. The gardener had a limited arrangement already available for ordinary decoration. The new planting choice did not need to bear every hope for visible color on its own.

season_garden_05_012.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_05_012.text: “I would like a tree that can belong to another child's summer later,” Yue said. “But I don't want to make today's patients wait because I prefer the idea of patience.” She heard how carefully she was trying to become fair and almost laughed at herself. Qiu said a young tree could be a real present thing too, if nobody forced it to look like the old one. The gardener pointed to its potential safe position, away from the route, and explained how its long establishment would be checked by staff.

season_garden_05_013.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_013.text: The bench owner listened to both possibilities and said she did not want the new planting named after her husband without asking his family. She also did not want it named after the fallen tree as if one trunk had an identity a replacement had to inherit. The garden could plant something useful and let people give it their own ordinary affection. Her son arrived with another small onion sack and agreed. He said a new tree should not be required to carry every old sadness before it had grown its first sound root.

season_garden_05_014.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_014.text: Qiu's sister sent another brief written suggestion through the ordinary family arrangement Qiu had chosen. She favored bright annuals because she could identify their colors from an indoor chair and disliked being told to admire a promise. Qiu read the words aloud only because her sister had permitted her to share that suggestion with the garden. The rest of the note stayed folded. Yue smiled at the phrase and wondered what a young tree might look like to a person whose body had made every promise expensive.

season_garden_05_015.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_015.text: Ren Qiao asked to speak before the debate made patients into imaginary examples. “Ask the people who want to offer an opinion,” he said. “Some may want flowers. Some may want a tree. Some may be tired of being represented by a bed of either kind.” He was not assigning a clinical preference to the choice. Staff could invite ordinary voluntary comments on the space without turning care into a ballot. The garden's responsible owners had agreed the viable options; Yue's selected first use would be a bounded maintenance decision.

season_garden_05_016.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_016.text: A woman waiting near the apothecary said flowers reminded her of markets and made the room feel less like an institution. A man leaving the dining hall said he liked watching a young tree's buds change because it gave him something to notice when he arrived early. Neither wanted to argue with the other. Qiu wrote the volunteered preferences as they were, with no names attached because the work did not need them. Yue asked what the current route users needed first. Clear space remained their most immediate answer.

season_garden_05_017.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_017.text: The pinwheel child's grandmother chose to sit under the new checked shade for a short visit that afternoon, after staff arranged it within her current plan. The child brought the empty stick and told her it would become a boat mast. She said a boat needed a hull as well as a mast. He answered that the hull was a problem for tomorrow. Her laugh came easily, followed by visible tiredness. Staff supported the agreed return indoors when she wanted it. Nobody asked her to lengthen the visit because the bench looked so successful.

season_garden_05_018.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_018.text: Before leaving the court, she volunteered that she liked yellow flowers. Then she asked whether somebody would bring her a picture if she was indoors when they opened. Yue said staff could discuss an ordinary chosen way to share the view, but she did not promise that annuals would bloom or that the bed would be selected. The grandmother said she understood. She had planted enough beans to know liking a thing did not make it happen. Qiu looked at the folded plan and became quieter.

season_garden_05_019.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_019.text: Yue asked the grandmother whether a young plum would disappoint her. The woman said she could enjoy a tree and still wish for yellow flowers. Her appetite for the world did not fit the helpers' two tidy boxes. She wanted to return indoors now, and that preference outranked their wish to complete the discussion. They thanked her and stepped out of the route. Qiu said afterward that the answer made choosing harder. Yue said it made representing the choice easier: neither path had to pretend the other desire was false.

season_garden_05_020.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_020.text: The gardener gave the helpers light preparation that served either viable option while the decision remained open: sorting the approved empty containers, checking the readable labels and keeping the safe bed's approach clear. No seed was sown and no tree purchased before the selection. Yue worked at the supported table with the same ordinary shoulder limits. Qiu separated cracked containers staff had deemed unsuitable. Their hands could do concrete work while a question stayed unanswered, which both found easier than sitting around a plan until they had earned certainty.

season_garden_05_021.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_021.text: A shallow bowl slipped from Qiu's dry fingers and struck the low tray. It did not break, but its sound startled the people nearby. She apologized for the noise and checked the bowl with the gardener before using it. Her hands were tired enough that she had been trying to complete one more stack by instinct. The agreed break was almost due. Yue did not diagnose the fatigue or tell her how to feel about it. She asked whether Qiu wanted to bring the break forward and confirm the changed order with the responsible worker.

season_garden_05_022.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_05_022.text: “Yes,” Qiu said, surprising herself by saying it without a joke. They took the agreed break together after securing the light work. Qiu admitted that the flower choice had begun to feel like defending the people who needed a good day now. That had made every hesitation seem cruel. Yue said her own tree preference could become a way of defending a future nobody had asked her to defend. The two women sat with their cups while the actual people around them ate, rested and complained about ordinary weather.

season_garden_05_023.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_023.text: At the neighboring table, the bench owner and her son disagreed over how much onion belonged in the afternoon greens. Their argument was loud enough to make the painter's remembered blue bird seem part of an easier day. Yue smiled toward her cup rather than toward them. She had been using their loss as an example of careful remembrance, and here they were living a meal that had no interest in becoming her argument. Qiu said she liked the sound of a family disagreement that was only about onions.

season_garden_05_024.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_024.text: Su asked what information remained necessary before Yue chose. The gardener had confirmed viable stock, safe placement, actual water and ordinary post-term maintenance. Material costs and purchase authority were clear. The comments had revealed wishes without creating a clinical ranking. Yue said she wanted to see the proposed young tree before choosing, if the supplier and gardener permitted an ordinary look. Qiu wanted to see the actual annual seed information and expected mature size. Neither inspection would make the future fully available, but both could replace an image with something real.

season_garden_05_025.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_025.text: The gardener brought the supplier's present description and a small branch sample from the suitable stock inspection, not an unpurchased tree dragged into the work room as if acceptance had already happened. He showed the expected young size and its establishment needs. Qiu looked at the spare shape and said it would be difficult to see from the indoor chair at first. Yue agreed. The tree's useful future would begin as a modest present thing requiring staff care, not a miniature version of the lost crown.

season_garden_05_026.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_026.text: The annual packet's approved information described mature height and the intended modest sowing amount. Qiu found the estimate smaller than the bright mass she had imagined. The gardener said a viable small bed could be expanded in a future season only with its own actual space, water and maintenance agreement. Yue asked whether the annuals would crowd the route if they grew well. The plan kept their mature size within the safe bed. Qiu traced the small boundary with a finger and accepted that useful color need not fill every visible gap.

season_garden_05_027.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_05_027.text: “I keep making both plans too large in my head,” Yue said. “The tree becomes the old tree; the flowers become an entire summer.” Qiu laughed because she had done the same. The gardener said an inspected plan often looked disappointing beside imagination and satisfying beside a real usable afternoon. He offered no grand philosophy after that. He returned to the actual soil condition while the women sorted their containers. Yue liked the practical permission to be disappointed without demanding the plan become less honest.

season_garden_05_028.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_028.text: The owner asked whether the selected planting would need to disturb the bench's present position. Neither viable option did. The safe small bed and route had been planned together under the gardener's inspection. She looked relieved. Her seat had only just returned, and she did not want the new choice to make it provisional again. Qiu said that was a useful request to hear before deciding. Yue added it to the maintenance conditions without treating the owner as hostile to change. A repaired comfort could deserve time to remain ordinary.

season_garden_05_029.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_029.text: A visitor left a parcel beside the work shelf and asked the helpers to hold it until evening. Qiu said the shelf belonged to the current garden work and they would be leaving at the session's end. Staff directed the visitor to the proper ordinary arrangement if one was available. The parcel did not become their custody through proximity. Yue was grateful for Qiu's quick clear refusal. The garden had enough real choices without every object set down near them acquiring a promise nobody had actually made.

season_garden_05_030.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_030.text: They prepared the final empty containers and returned uncertain pieces to the gardener's separate stock. Yue copied no future planting date onto the labels. Qiu wrote the actual inspected count for either plan's available containers. The work stayed useful under both possible choices. A tray was ready and a decision was not. Neither condition invalidated the other. Su told them there was still enough ordinary time to choose before the treasurer's purchase authorization, and no need to rush merely because the table looked neatly arranged.

season_garden_05_031.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_031.text: The kitchen woman went to sit on her checked bench for ten minutes before supper work. She invited Yue to take the available chair beside her, then asked whether Qiu wanted the other one. Both accepted during the agreed pause in their light assignment. The new shade held the afternoon glare without making the air cool. The woman said her husband would have complained about that too. Qiu asked what he had enjoyed. She answered that he liked complaining while other people stayed long enough to argue.

season_garden_05_032.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_032.text: Yue heard affection in the answer and remembered how often she had tried to make company helpful. Sometimes somebody wanted a visitor to bring no improvement, only enough time for a familiar irritation to finish its small arc. She told the woman she thought the blue bird's wings still looked like leaves. The owner said they were obviously wings and that Yue needed better eyes. Qiu laughed so hard she startled a sparrow from the edge of the shelter. For a minute the court was a place where nobody required them to be wise.

season_garden_05_033.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_033.text: The sparrow landed beyond the safe bed and pecked a dry husk. Qiu asked whether annual seeds would need protection while they established. The gardener's actual plan included suitable ordinary covering and checks within the maintenance rota. A tree would have different protection and support needs under staff's planting work. Yue looked at the bird, whose ordinary appetite did not make it a villain in the plan. The garden belonged to more lives than its users, and caring for planted growth would involve managing that shared space in specific ways.

season_garden_05_034.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_034.text: The bench owner said she did not want traps for the birds. The gardener confirmed the approved plan used ordinary nonharmful seed protection suitable for the small bed, with no traps promised or needed. Yue did not generalize that a garden could always avoid difficult pest decisions; this plan had its own feasible measures. Qiu asked to see the covering when the actual planting began. The gardener said he would show the responsible helpers their permitted light task then, rather than turn today's decision meeting into a demonstration of work not yet accepted.

season_garden_05_035.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_035.text: The grandmother's visiting adult came from the room with the child's empty stick. She said the grandmother had enjoyed the short outdoor visit and was resting again. She offered no clinical explanation to the helpers. The child wanted to draw yellow flowers on his proposed boat because a tree would be too large for the hull. Yue told him a drawing could fit things the hull could not carry. He asked whether that was cheating. Qiu said it sounded like what drawings were especially good at doing.

season_garden_05_036.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_036.text: He drew one crooked flower on a permitted spare scrap while his adult waited. The stem was so long that it resembled a sail rope. He showed Yue, then decided it would be a rope after all. Qiu admired the change with the sincerity of somebody who knew how stubborn a finished first idea could become. The child took the scrap home. His grandmother's wish for yellow flowers remained hers, and his drawing had followed its own ordinary path into a boat nobody needed to build on the garden's schedule.

season_garden_05_037.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_05_037.text: “Perhaps I should ask my sister what she wants to complain about when she comes,” Qiu said after the family left. Yue said that sounded less burdensome than promising a perfect visit. Qiu answered that her sister would probably complain about being asked such a carefully useful question. They both laughed. The protected family dates remained on Qiu's calendar. She would not take on extra garden sessions to pay for a planting preference or prove the choice had made her generous enough to deserve the time away.

season_garden_05_038.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_038.text: Su returned to the planting plan once the ordinary work was ready for handover. The next session could begin the chosen option's light preparation after actual authorization and staff purchase, if weather and stock remained as confirmed. The unchosen option would remain a possible future enquiry rather than a hidden second promise within this ten-week reserve. Yue felt the relief and cost of that boundary. She could choose without having to arrange both outcomes through extra private effort, and somebody's present wish would still remain unanswered.

season_garden_05_039.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_05_039.text: “The tree matters to me,” Yue said. “The flowers matter too. I don't want choosing to make me pretend otherwise.” Qiu said a preference could remain honest if it named what it gave up. The gardener said neither option would bear that sacrifice alone: existing decoration, safe seating and the ordinary people returning would still make the court more than one planting. Yue looked at the empty safe bed. It could hold an actual chosen use without being required to become the entire emotional future of the orchard.

season_garden_05_040.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_040.text: They each completed the fifth three-hour session and received their agreed three copper, bringing garden wages to fifteen copper each. Thirty copper of the labor reserve had now been paid; the six-copper bench repair remained the only completed materials expenditure. One hundred twenty-four copper remained held in the garden reserve before any new planting purchase. Su kept the proposed three- or eight-copper cost as an authorization awaiting the real selection and acceptance, rather than spending both alternatives in an account because they had both been discussed.

season_garden_05_041.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_041.text: Before choosing, Yue walked to the permitted viewing point for the cleared old crown. The remaining ground work still had its own closure, and she did not cross it to make the visit feel more complete. The sky gap looked less startling now and no less empty. She could hear the owner's knife from the kitchen. Qiu joined her at the safe point without asking what conclusion the view was meant to produce. They looked for a while and returned when the table's ordinary decision time arrived.

season_garden_05_042.speaker: narrator
season_garden_05_042.text: The two viable plans lay beside one another, small enough that each still had real limits. The annuals offered possible color within the present season, under ordinary uncertainty and actual care. The young plum offered a living start for future shade, without borrowing a mature crown or promising this season's relief. Staff maintenance, safe placement, water and price had been confirmed for either modest use. Yue's next choice would direct the first planting. The other wish would remain visible in the people who had spoken it.

season_garden_planting_choice.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_choice.text: Yue would choose the garden's first actual planting use. Both modest options had confirmed staff care, safe placement, water and a stated authorized cost. Seasonal annuals might bring visible color within this season, without a guaranteed bloom date. One young plum would begin a longer living future, without this season's missing shade. The unchosen option would remain an unaccepted possibility. The decision could preserve an honest loss instead of promising both futures through invisible extra labor or money.

choices.text: Begin the modest seasonal flower bed.
Begin with one young plum under staff care.

season_garden_planting_annuals_01.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_planting_annuals_01.text: “Begin with the seasonal flowers,” Yue said. “I want a modest patch of possible color in the time this garden is actually being used now. The young tree remains a worthwhile future enquiry, with its own ground and care question. It isn't included in this purchase.” She felt the choice land with a small ache. The future tree she had imagined would not appear because she had privately continued loving it. Choosing one real plan meant letting the other remain honestly unperformed in the present.

season_garden_planting_annuals_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_02.text: Qiu did not cheer as though Yue had admitted the quick method superior. She asked the gardener to retain the actual germination uncertainty beside the purchase authorization. The annual packet's confirmed price and suitable light planting materials came to three copper, payable from the garden materials allowance after the real purchase. The treasurer approved that bounded authorization and staff accepted the planting under their existing care plan. No money entered either helper's purse, and no second option was bought to make their disappointment disappear.

season_garden_planting_annuals_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_planting_annuals_03.text: “I want to say we will have flowers for the grandmother,” Qiu admitted. “But I know what that sentence would steal from the weather.” Yue said they could tell her the actual selection and ask whether she wanted an ordinary update when anything emerged. Staff would handle that chosen communication. Qiu nodded. Her preference had become a plan with uncertainty, not a brighter excuse to guarantee the result. The people she wanted to serve could remain visible without their wishes becoming dates a seed was required to obey.

season_garden_planting_annuals_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_04.text: The gardener outlined the actual next light tasks if the present stock and weather held: prepare the identified containers, label the confirmed sowing date after it happened, and assist with approved light covering while staff managed the ground and water schedule. Yue asked which movements were suitable for her shoulder. The gardener would assign table work and limited comfortable movements within the present clinical work limits. Qiu asked where her speed would be useful. He said clear preparation could make sowing orderly; hurrying the soil would not.

season_garden_planting_annuals_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_05.text: Yue went to the kitchen woman and described the selected annual plan at its real scale. The woman said she liked yellow but did not want every flower to be called a memorial. Yue agreed. The new planting would remain an ordinary public garden use unless the responsible people separately chose another designation. The owner's husband could belong to her story without becoming the reason every visitor had to admire the bed. She tapped the blue bird and said this small private joke already carried enough of him for today.

season_garden_planting_annuals_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_06.text: The woman's son asked whether annuals would vanish after summer. The gardener explained their actual seasonal cycle and ordinary end-of-season handling. A bed that changed with the season was not necessarily a failed attempt at permanence. The son said he liked that. His mother said she might miss the flowers anyway. Their answers did not cancel each other. Yue heard a future small grief being acknowledged before it existed, and wondered whether temporary joy could become easier to accept when nobody required it to promise a lifetime.

season_garden_planting_annuals_07.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_planting_annuals_07.text: “I chose this partly because I am tired of making every good thing wait for a future strong enough to justify it,” Yue told Qiu privately. “That doesn't make the waiting useless. I just wanted a present use to count.” Qiu looked at her more carefully than the practical selection had required. “I wanted the flowers for a similar reason,” she said, “and also because they are bright.” Yue laughed with relief. A morally serious choice could include the unembarrassed fact that somebody liked yellow.

season_garden_planting_annuals_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_08.text: They asked staff whether the grandmother wanted to hear the planting choice today. Her present answer was yes, briefly, through the staff member already attending her. Yue and Qiu did not enter uninvited or seek a grateful response. Staff returned that she was pleased the bed might have yellow flowers and wanted to be told about actual emergence rather than every proposed step. Qiu wrote that communication preference where the responsible staff could use it, without adding any clinical information or assuming the choice improved her health.

season_garden_planting_annuals_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_09.text: The child heard from his accompanying adult and asked whether the first flower could belong to his boat. The garden's ordinary picking rules would still apply; a new planting did not make every blossom available. Yue said he could draw a yellow flower whenever he wanted, and they could later ask the gardener about any permitted use of real flowers. He decided the drawn flower would need less water. Qiu laughed. The seed packet had acquired anticipation without being emptied into every person's imagined possession.

season_garden_planting_annuals_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_10.text: Before leaving, Yue checked the tree enquiry would not appear on the helper schedule as hidden extra work. Su confirmed that no young tree had been accepted, purchased or promised under this selection. The garden owners could revisit that possible use in another real arrangement if they wanted it. Yue let the plan go. The feeling resembled setting down a tool that was still useful but not hers to carry today. Qiu asked whether she wanted a copy of the annual plan. Yue said yes, limited to the actual light assignments.

season_garden_planting_annuals_11.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_planting_annuals_11.text: “I am glad you chose the flowers,” Qiu said at the gate. “I don't want that to become a debt you owe me next time.” Yue answered that she had not chosen them as a concession to the entire quick method. Qiu smiled. “Good. I would make an unbearable winner if you let me.” Their rivalry had survived a shared preference. The next disagreement could arrive from a different need, and neither woman would be required to spend this choice defending a permanent side.

season_garden_planting_annuals_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_12.text: The three-copper purchase authorization stayed with the garden treasurer and the accepted actual planting plan stayed with the gardener. Payment and sowing would be recorded only when performed. Thirty-four copper remained in the materials allowance at this session's close; the selected amount was committed but not yet spent. The women each carried fifteen copper earned through their five completed sessions. Yue left the protected home hours on her calendar and Qiu left her sister's dates untouched. A desired bright bed did not purchase their entire future availability.

season_garden_planting_annuals_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_annuals_13.text: As Yue walked home, she pictured the small yellow flowers and then replaced the imagined certainty with the empty bed she had actually seen. The bed was ready for its staff-directed next work, not already in bloom. She could want a future appearance without reporting it into existence. The young tree remained a loss within the choice, a useful other plan not taken today. She let both feelings accompany her for part of the road, then turned her attention to the ordinary supper she still needed before sleep.

season_garden_planting_plum_01.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_planting_plum_01.text: “Begin with the young plum,” Yue said. “I want one modest living start for a future garden, in the safe bed where staff have confirmed its care. It will not provide this season's missing shade. The flowering annuals remain a worthwhile future enquiry, outside this purchase.” She felt Qiu's disappointment before Qiu spoke. The wish for color in the present had not become false because Yue chose another viable use. She would keep that unanswered wish visible without secretly promising to deliver it after hours.

season_garden_planting_plum_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_02.text: Qiu asked the gardener to state the young tree's actual present size and establishment needs beside the purchase authorization. The suitable stock and required planting materials came to eight copper, payable from the garden materials allowance after the real purchase. The treasurer approved that bounded authorization and staff accepted its maintenance under their existing ordinary rota and water plan. No money entered either helper's purse. The garden had agreed to care for one young tree, not to purchase a mature crown or borrow the old tree's remembered summers.

season_garden_planting_plum_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_planting_plum_03.text: “I wanted color for people here now,” Qiu said. “I still do.” Yue answered that the limited existing decoration could remain under its owner's consent and the safe route conditions, but it would not be described as the annual bed they had declined. The gardener showed where the young plum would be visible without obstructing the turn. Qiu looked at its small possible shape. “Then I will try to notice what it is now,” she said, “instead of punishing it for failing to be the tree you mean later.”

season_garden_planting_plum_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_04.text: The gardener outlined the actual next work if the confirmed stock and weather remained suitable. Qualified staff would manage the ground, transplanting, support and establishment checks. The helpers could prepare approved light ties, labels and permitted surface protection under instruction. Yue's shoulder limits would shape the assigned movements; she would not carry the tree or dig the heavier hole. Qiu asked whether her gauge had a useful task. The gardener named a limited measurement for the support preparation after his own plan was marked, giving her speed a concrete place to help.

season_garden_planting_plum_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_05.text: Yue described the selected young plum to the bench owner without calling it a replacement for her husband or the old tree's life. The woman looked relieved. “Let it be a new inconvenient tree,” she said. “It will have leaves to sweep and somebody will complain about them.” Qiu laughed. The owner wanted the bench to remain in its checked position and its blue bird to stay visible. The gardener confirmed the approved planting would respect both. A future living thing could begin beside existing ordinary preferences rather than erase them.

season_garden_planting_plum_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_06.text: The owner's son asked whether he could see the young stock when it arrived through the gardener's actual arrangement. The gardener agreed to an ordinary permitted viewing after staff received it and before helpers' light work, if timing allowed. The son said he had once planted a small tree with his father and had forgotten that memory until now. His mother said she remembered the argument about the hole. Yue did not make that resemblance the public meaning of the new planting. It had arrived as a family's own unexpected story.

season_garden_planting_plum_07.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_planting_plum_07.text: “I chose this partly because I want to stay interested in a future I may not be here to finish,” Yue told Qiu privately. “That doesn't give me the right to spend somebody else's present comfort on the image.” Qiu asked whether the confirmed staff care had answered that concern. Yue said it had made the modest plan possible; the unchosen flower wish still hurt. Qiu nodded. “I can respect a choice better when it doesn't tell me the thing I wanted was childish.”

season_garden_planting_plum_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_08.text: They asked staff whether the grandmother wanted a brief ordinary update about the planting choice. Her present answer was yes, through the staff member already attending her. She said she liked plum trees and still liked yellow flowers. Yue heard the reply without trying to convert it into wholehearted approval. The patient had not been asked to bless the helpers' preference as part of receiving care. Qiu suggested they could continue sharing the existing safe decorations when requested. Staff kept that possibility inside each person's own actual visiting wishes.

season_garden_planting_plum_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_09.text: The child heard that a young plum might arrive and asked if he could climb it. The gardener's ordinary protection rules would prevent that, especially while the tree established; the damaged old tree area also remained closed. Yue said he could look at its buds from the permitted route if he wanted. He thought buds sounded less exciting than climbing, then asked whether they looked like small boat sails. Qiu said he could decide after actually seeing them. A disappointing limit still left room for a question.

season_garden_planting_plum_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_10.text: Before leaving, Yue checked that the annual enquiry had not become a hidden promise in the helpers' remaining sessions. Su confirmed that no seasonal flower bed had been accepted, bought or promised through this selection. The garden owners could consider another real arrangement later if resources and care supported it. Yue let the flower packet remain a possible other use rather than something she had to rescue with private money. Qiu folded her sister's color suggestion and kept it among family notes, where an unchosen idea could still be loved.

season_garden_planting_plum_11.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_planting_plum_11.text: “I will probably complain about how slowly the tree changes,” Qiu said at the gate. Yue said she would probably ask whether Qiu had eaten before the complaint. Qiu laughed and asked for an ordinary update on the actual planting date, since anticipation itself could otherwise become a deadline in her head. Their rivalry had survived different preferences without requiring a winner to acquire the other's loyalty. They had a shared finite maintenance arrangement, two separate lives and a new tree plan whose care belonged to the people who had actually accepted it.

season_garden_planting_plum_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_12.text: The eight-copper purchase authorization stayed with the garden treasurer and the accepted transplanting plan stayed with the responsible gardener. Payment and planting would be recorded only when performed. Thirty-four copper remained in the materials allowance at the session's close; the selected amount was committed but not yet spent. Each woman carried fifteen copper actually earned through five completed sessions. Yue's protected home hours and Qiu's sister visit remained beyond the garden's claim. A future tree had not bought its helpers unlimited hands or converted their wages into a donation.

season_garden_planting_plum_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_planting_plum_13.text: On the way home, Yue pictured the young plum as the modest thing the gardener had described, then caught herself enlarging it into summer shade. She returned to the empty safe bed she had actually seen. The tree might establish there through its staff-owned plan, with ordinary uncertainty and checks. The annuals remained a bright other future unperformed in this choice. She let the wish for them remain without changing her selection in secret, and turned toward the supper her present body still needed before thinking about another season.
